newsitem.title: USA: Clinton intervenes to help high school band.
newsitem.headline: Clinton intervenes to help high school band.

text.p: A high school marching band that hoped in vain to strut in President Bill Clinton's inaugural parade will be involved in the Jan. 20 celebration after all, the White House said Wednesday.

The Cody, Wyo. band's plight came to Clinton's attention through the Washington Post, which said in a front-page story Wednesday that its 94 teenage members had expected to perform at the inaugural but, because of politics, a high school band from the Democratic bastion of Jackson had been chosen to play for the Democratic president instead.

Enter Clinton, a former high school band member. "The president saw that story this morning and the president wants that story to have a happy ending," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.
McCurry said the Cody band would be involved in the inaugural, although "not necessarily" in the parade, which is limited to 24 of the 165 bands that applied.
Cody school superintendent Alan Hafer said in a telephone interview the band had been informed it would play at the Navy Monument in Washington and "our whole community is delighted."

Hafer said the episode had been a good learning experience for the students involved. "What they've learned is that the American government, from President Clinton on through to the people setting up the inaugural, are very human and very responsive," he said.
